your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: $444 cash. Vermont blocks p4's light blue, so it's good leverage. Don't give p4 a set cheaply, since they have $1712 and would build at once. I'd only trade Vermont for Atlantic plus a lot of cash, or for something that completes a set for me. Still want Marvin for yellow. Baltic is the first to mortgage if I need cash.

Vermont completes p4's light blue, and p4 has $1512 to build right away, so cash alone isn't enough. If I get Atlantic I'll hold 2 of the 3 yellows (Marvin is still unowned), plus $350 to rebuild. Don't drop below Atlantic plus about $250.

Giving p4 a set they can build on right away is a big deal, so I have to get a path to a set back. Atlantic gives me 2 of the 3 yellows, and Marvin is still unowned. My floor is Atlantic + about $200. Turn down cash-only offers unless they go far higher, around $700 or more.
Yellow is 2/3 for me, red would only be 1/3, so a fair swap should favor me. I'd accept Indiana plus about $400. Otherwise I keep the yellows.
States blocks p2's pink set, so it's leverage. Ask Indiana plus cash or more for it. Still want Marvin for yellow. Keep about $550 as a buffer against the light blues and Dark Blue.
States blocks p2's pinks, and Virginia is still unowned, so selling it is risky. I'll only sell for a big premium. I'd accept about $280 or more. I'm short on cash ($346), so extra cash helps too.
I need cash, since the light-blue rents are $450-500 and I only have $346. If p2 rejects again I'll take something around $200-230. One more push is low-risk.
$596 now. No trade gets me a set, so keep the cash as a buffer against the light blues and Dark Blue. Still want Marvin, NC and Penn. If cash runs short, mortgage Baltic first.

Marvin completes my yellows, so it's the most valuable thing for me on the board. Go up in small steps. I'd pay up to about $400 and still keep roughly $200 plus what I can raise by mortgaging. Above $450 only if I have to, to stop a block.
Final bid. If I win, I mortgage Pacific, Illinois and Baltic for about $300 and build yellows. If p4 goes higher, I drop out: p4 ends up with about $130 cash, which still helps me.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on PENNSYLVANIA_AVENUE in the current auction.

I have $398 and several unmortgaged properties. I need to complete the pink and red groups. The orange group is split. I am considering a bid of $151 against p4's $150.

p1 has dropped out. No player currently holds a green monopoly. p3 owns Pacific Avenue, so acquiring Pennsylvania would leave them with two greens and still need North Carolina. The property lists for $320 but pays only $28 rent. p4 has $634 cash and fully built light blues.

p3 has only $147 cash. They own a complete yellow monopoly but cannot afford to build houses yet. They previously declined to buy Pennsylvania Avenue outright because they could not cover the $320 price.

p3 cannot outbid the $151 minimum with only $147 cash. They remain listed as an active bidder, but they likely cannot raise their bid further.

p3 will drop out. The auction is now between me and p4.

I should not overpay for a property that does not complete a set. My priority is buying Virginia to finish the pink monopoly. p4 is the biggest threat with fully built light blues and $634 cash.

p1 owns Park Place and Boardwalk but only $46 cash, so they cannot build more houses. p4's bid of $150 is a speculative purchase at less than half the list price. If I let p4 win, they would gain a green tile that is not a complete set.

I cannot complete a green set by buying this property. p4 might raise the bid again. I should keep enough cash to purchase Virginia.

I have blocked the orange group. p4 owns St. James and I own Tennessee, so they cannot complete that set.

My priority is Virginia at $160 to finish the pink monopoly. I will not bid on Pennsylvania to stop p4 from acquiring a green tile that does not complete any set.

p3 previously warned p4 that blocking costs money. I could bid $151 and win the property, but that would leave me with only $247 cash and just $87 left after buying Virginia. That is too thin. Dropping out is safer.

A stranded green has rent and trade value, but I need liquidity. I will not raise the bid to overpay. p4 might push the price higher to deny p3, yet that is not worth the risk.

I cannot afford a 4-house light blue hit without mortgaging. Boardwalk at three houses costs $1400, and Park Place at two houses costs $500, so I would need to mortgage to cover either.

Raising the bid to pressure p4 is risky. They might drop out and leave me with the property, as happened with Marvin at $450.

p4 is bidding for value, not just to block. A $151 purchase would leave a dead green with only $247 cash. The property's mortgage value is $160, so buying it for $151 and mortgaging immediately would yield a $9 profit.

Mortgaging the property to recover cash is too risky and complex. I will drop out of the auction. I will keep my public message brief and avoid revealing my Virginia priority.
